thread:
Sam: Quick sync — Vertis Health signed LOI, they're asking for customer-managed egress + BGP peering with our on-prem package. Sales needs clear acceptance criteria before contract.
Priya: Let's map requirements: static egress IPs, prefix advertisement, health checks, metrics export (Prometheus), DNS behavior, failover policy.
Marco: Edge cases: dual-homed routers, overlapping ASNs, NAT64/IPv6 translation, MTU mismatches. Also legal constraint: can we accept customer-provided routes? Contract will need indemnity.
Elaine: From runtime POV we can support passive BGP (monitoring) and static routes today. Full BGP peering + route injection needs route validation, RPKI/routing-policy checks. Roughly 3 sprints to build safe controls.
Connor: Can we enumerate launch gates? e.g., 1) BGP test harness with emulated peers, 2) stable egress IPs >= 24h, 3) observability: route-change alerting, 4) failover SLO < 30s? Not sure on SLO.
Priya: Proposed acceptance criteria bullets:
- Documented egress IP/CIDR announced to customer
- Option for customer-managed BGP peering or static route
- Automatic opt-in fallback to cloud egress if peering fails (customer-controlled)
- Audit logs of all route updates (who/when)
- TLS/KMS handshake for certs stored in customer KMS
Elaine: Note: fallback to cloud egress is sensitive for regulated customers — should be opt-in and in contract. Fallback SLA needs to be explicit.
Marco: Implementation notes — example FRR config snippet we tested:
```bgp
neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 64512
neighbor 10.0.0.2 ebgp-multihop 2
!
address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.0.2.0/24
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 activate
exit-address-family
```
devops-bot: Checklist created: /checklists/customer-egress-v1 — test plan + lab topology added.
Sam: Plan: Priya to draft acceptance doc for Sales/Legal by EOD Friday; Elaine+Marco to estimate dev effort & risk; Connor to propose test harness. @devops-bot schedule a 60m sync next Tues.
Priya: Quick Q — should we require BGP MD5 auth and TTL-security? Customer specifically requested MD5.
Marco: Yes — require MD5 (or TCP-AO) and add overlap-check to acceptance. No overlapping customer CIDRs without manual signoff.
Elaine: Rough estimates: 6w dev + 2w ops + 1 sprint dedicated on-prem QA. Known risk: cert rotation + KMS integration complexity.
Connor: I'll spin up a 3-node FRR topology in lab and validate route flaps/failover, ETA Tue.
Sam: :thumbsup: Thanks. I'll loop in Nadia (Legal) if we need contract language. Adding this thread to the initiative board and linking the PRD when ready.
